items.prompt: Where is the weak letter in qāla (root q-w-l)?
options: In the middle: an ajwaf verb
At the start: a mithāl verb
At the end: a nāqiṣ verb
items.explanation: The wāw is the second root letter, so qāla is ajwaf.

items.prompt: What happens to the wāw of this verb in the present tense?
items.explanation: In the mithāl of the pattern faʿala yafʿilu, the wāw drops in the present: yaʿidu.

options: nāqiṣ: weak in the last letter
mithāl: weak in the first letter
items.explanation: Ramā comes from r-m-y: the weak letter is the third.
